message.content:
You are the final reviewer for Phase B of an implementation plan: a backwards-compatible bump of the existing `otel-collector` Terraform internal-module.

This task is **review-only** — no file modifications, no git operations, no terraform apply.

## What was changed in Phase B

Read the current state of these files in `/Users/steve.briggs/projects/IAC/terraform/internal-modules/kubernetes/monitoring/otel-collector/`:

- `variables.tf` — should have NEW additive variables `downstream_endpoint` (string, default `""`) and `downstream_protocol` (string, default `"otlp/grpc"`, with a validation block).
- `otelconfig.tf` — should be refactored to conditionally render either `exporters.datadog/exporter` (default) or `exporters.otlp` (when `downstream_endpoint != ""`). Pipeline exporter lists swap based on the same conditional.
- `main.tf` — `kubernetes_manifest.otel-collector` (the ExternalSecret resource for the Datadog API key) should have `count = var.downstream_endpoint == "" ? 1 : 0`. The `extraEnvsFrom` block on the processor helm release should be a conditional list (mounting the Datadog secret in default mode, empty list in downstream mode).
- `examples/downstream/` — three new files (versions.tf, main.tf, README.md) demonstrating downstream mode.
- `README.md` — newly created module docs.
- `lbconfig.tf` — should NOT have semantic changes (only auto-formatting fixes if any).

## Verification checks to run

- [ ] **Check 1: Backwards compatibility — direct mode is byte-identical to before.**

  Reproduce the ad-hoc plan-render verification from Task B4. Build a tempdir, instantiate the module with NO `downstream_endpoint` (or `= ""`). Inspect the rendered processor helm release config:
  - `exporters.datadog/exporter.api.site` = `"datadoghq.com"` (unchanged)
  - `exporters.datadog/exporter.api.key` = `"${env:DD_API_KEY}"` (unchanged escape)
  - `exporters.datadog/exporter.sending_queue.storage` = `"file_storage/persistent_queue"` (unchanged)
  - Pipelines: traces=`[datadog/connector, datadog/exporter]`, logs=`[datadog/exporter]`, metrics=`[datadog/exporter]` (unchanged)
  - `extraEnvsFrom` contains `secretRef.name = "otel-collector"` (unchanged)
  - `kubernetes_manifest.otel-collector[0]` planned for create (count=1) (unchanged)

- [ ] **Check 2: Downstream mode renders correctly.**

  Same tempdir technique with `downstream_endpoint = "http://vector.vector.svc.cluster.local:4317"`:
  - `exporters.otlp.endpoint` = the URL passed
  - `exporters.otlp.tls.insecure` = `true`
  - `exporters.otlp.sending_queue.enabled` = `true`, `queue_size` = `5000`
  - `exporters.otlp.retry_on_failure` block present with the expected values
  - `exporters.datadog/exporter` ABSENT
  - Pipelines: traces=`[datadog/connector, otlp]`, logs=`[otlp]`, metrics=`[otlp]`
  - `extraEnvsFrom` empty list `[]`
  - `kubernetes_manifest.otel-collector` NOT planned (count=0)

- [ ] **Check 3: `terraform fmt -check -recursive`** at module root. Exit 0.

- [ ] **Check 4: `terraform validate`** at module root. `Success! The configuration is valid.`

- [ ] **Check 5: examples/downstream validate.** Inside `examples/downstream/`, run `terraform init -backend=false && terraform validate`. Both must pass.

- [ ] **Check 6: Spot-check `lbconfig.tf` for semantic drift.** The LB tier should be untouched. Compare against any older version available via `git diff v1.0.5 -- lbconfig.tf` IF and ONLY IF you're absolutely sure that `git diff` is read-only and won't touch state. If you don't want to risk it, skip this check and report `lbconfig.tf` was reformatted but not semantically changed (per B3/B4 implementer reports).

- [ ] **Check 7: Spot-check `otelconfig.tf` for unintended drift.** The `connectors`, `processors`, `receivers`, `extensions`, `service.telemetry`, and pipeline `processors` lists should match what was there pre-Phase B. The only changes should be: exporters map (now derived from a local), and the three pipeline exporter lists (now derived from locals).

## Things to flag in the report

- Any check that fails or returns unexpected output.
- Any sign that perf-tuning values (`send_batch_max_size`, etc.) on the `otel-batch-size` branch were touched (they should NOT have been — those belong to the unmerged perf work).
- Confirmation that the cherry-pick path onto a v1.0.5 feature branch will be clean (i.e., the changes don't intermingle with perf-tuning lines).
- Any concerns or open questions for Sir Charles.

## Constraints

- **DO NOT run any git commands** that mutate state. `git diff` and `git log` are READ-ONLY and acceptable for verification, but no checkout, branch, commit, push, etc.
- **DO NOT** push, tag, open MRs.
- **DO NOT** run `terraform apply`.
- **DO NOT** modify any files. This is review-only.

## Report Format

- **Status:** APPROVED | ISSUES_FOUND | BLOCKED
- Each of the 7 checks: PASS / FAIL with one-line evidence.
- Any other concerns or notes for Sir Charles
- Recommendation for what to do next (open MR, fix issues, etc.)

content.content:
1	# otel-collector
2	
3	Two-tier OpenTelemetry collector module: a load-balancer deployment in front of a processor StatefulSet, exporting to Datadog by default or to a configurable OTLP downstream when `downstream_endpoint` is set.
4	
5	## Architecture
6	
7	Workloads emit OTLP to the load-balancer tier (Deployment), which distributes spans, metrics, and logs across the processor tier (StatefulSet) using consistent hashing. The processor tier enriches, batches, and exports telemetry. Persistent volumes on the processor nodes back the sending queue so in-flight data survives pod restarts.
8	
9	```
10	workloads (OTLP/gRPC or HTTP)
11	        |
12	        v
13	 otel-collector-lb  (Deployment, N replicas)
14	   loadbalancing exporter — consistent-hash routing
15	        |
16	        v
17	 otel-collector-processor  (StatefulSet, N replicas)
18	   batch / resourcedetection / k8sattributes
19	        |
20	        +-- [direct mode]      --> Datadog API
21	        +-- [downstream mode]  --> OTLP endpoint (e.g. Vector)
22	```
23	
24	## Modes
25	
26	### Direct mode (default — `downstream_endpoint = ""`)
27	
28	Behavior when `downstream_endpoint` is empty (the default):
29	
30	- The module creates a Kubernetes `ExternalSecret` that pulls the Datadog API key from Vault (`secret/data/saas/infrastructure/datadog-api-key`) and materialises it as the `otel-collector` Kubernetes Secret.
31	- The processor Helm release mounts that secret via `extraEnvsFrom`, making `DD_API_KEY` available to the collector process.
32	- The rendered collector config includes `exporters.datadog/exporter`; pipelines reference `[datadog/exporter]`. The traces pipeline additionally uses `datadog/connector` for APM stats.
33	
34	### Downstream mode (`downstream_endpoint = "http://..."`)
35	
36	Behavior when `downstream_endpoint` is non-empty (introduced in v1.1.0):
37	
38	- The `ExternalSecret` resource is **not** created — no Datadog API key is required or injected.
39	- The processor Helm release omits `extraEnvsFrom` for the Datadog secret.
40	- The rendered collector config includes `exporters.otlp` configured as follows:
41	  - `endpoint`: value of `var.downstream_endpoint`
42	  - `tls.insecure: true`
43	  - `sending_queue.queue_size: 5000`
44	  - `retry_on_failure.max_elapsed_time: "300s"`
45	- Pipelines reference `[otlp]` as the terminal exporter. The traces pipeline still keeps `datadog/connector` for APM stats passthrough but drops `datadog/exporter`.
46	
47	This mode is designed for routing through Vector (or any other OTLP-aware sink) — for example, to redact PII before forwarding to Datadog.
48	
49	## Inputs
50	
51	### Required
52	
53	| Name | Type | Description |
54	|------|------|-------------|
55	| `chart_version` | `string` | Version of the OTel collector Helm chart |
56	| `image_tag_version` | `string` | Image tag to use for the collector containers |
57	
58	### Optional
59	
60	| Name | Type | Default | Description |
61	|------|------|---------|-------------|
62	| `name` | `string` | `"otel-collector"` | Base name for created resources |
63	| `otel_image` | `string` | `registry.ic-ops.net/.../opentelemetry-collector-contrib` | Image repository for the processor tier |
64	| `otellb_image` | `string` | `registry.ic-ops.net/.../opentelemetry-collector` | Image repository for the LB tier |
65	| `otel_lb_replicas` | `number` | `3` | Replica count for the LB Deployment |
66	| `otel_collector_replicas` | `number` | `3` | Replica count for the processor StatefulSet |
67	| `otel_sa_name` | `string` | `"otel-collector-sa"` | ServiceAccount name for the processor StatefulSet |
68	| `otellb_sa_name` | `string` | `"otel-collector-lb-sa"` | ServiceAccount name for the LB Deployment |
69	| `otel_pv_size` | `string` | `"5Gi"` | PersistentVolume size for the processor queue storage |
70	| `otel_storage_class_name` | `string` | `"ebs-encrypted"` | StorageClass for the processor PersistentVolumeClaim |
71	| `sa_annotations` | `map(string)` | `{}` | Annotations to apply to both ServiceAccounts (e.g. IRSA role ARN) |
72	| `namespace` | `string` | `"opentelemetry"` | Kubernetes namespace for all resources |
73	| `annotations` | `map(string)` | `{}` | Annotations to apply to collector pods |
74	| `extra_args` | `list(string)` | `[]` | Extra CLI arguments for the processor collector container |
75	| `otellb_extra_args` | `list(string)` | `[]` | Extra CLI arguments for the LB collector container |
76	| `tags` | `map(any)` | `{}` | Tags to apply to created resources |
77	| `downstream_endpoint` | `string` | `""` | When non-empty, swap the terminal exporter to OTLP pointed at this endpoint. Empty preserves direct-to-Datadog behavior. |
78	| `downstream_protocol` | `string` | `"otlp/grpc"` | Wire protocol for the downstream OTLP exporter. Allowed: `otlp/grpc`, `otlp/http`. |
79	
80	## Outputs
81	
82	All outputs are prefixed with `helm_chart_lb_*` (load-balancer release) or `helm_chart_collector_*` (processor release).
83	
84	| Name | Description |
85	|------|-------------|
86	| `helm_chart_lb_status` | Helm release status for the LB tier |
87	| `helm_chart_lb_version` | Helm chart version for the LB tier |
88	| `helm_chart_lb_revision` | Helm revision number for the LB tier |
89	| `helm_chart_lb_app_version` | Application version for the LB tier |
90	| `helm_chart_lb_values` | Rendered Helm values for the LB tier |
91	| `helm_chart_collector_status` | Helm release status for the processor tier |
92	| `helm_chart_collector_version` | Helm chart version for the processor tier |
93	| `helm_chart_collector_revision` | Helm revision number for the processor tier |
94	| `helm_chart_collector_app_version` | Application version for the processor tier |
95	| `helm_chart_collector_values` | Rendered Helm values for the processor tier |
96	
97	## Usage
98	
99	### Direct mode (export to Datadog)
100	
101	```hcl
102	module "otel_collector" {
103	  source = "git@gitlab.infrastructure.immuta.io:infrastructure/terraform/internal-modules/kubernetes/monitoring/otel-collector.git?ref=v1.1.0"
104	
105	  chart_version     = "0.85.0"
106	  image_tag_version = "0.85.0"
107	
108	  # downstream_endpoint defaults to "" — direct-to-Datadog mode
109	}
110	```
111	
112	### Downstream mode (route through Vector for redaction)
113	
114	```hcl
115	module "otel_collector" {
116	  source = "git@gitlab.infrastructure.immuta.io:infrastructure/terraform/internal-modules/kubernetes/monitoring/otel-collector.git?ref=v1.1.0"
117	
118	  chart_version     = "0.85.0"
119	  image_tag_version = "0.85.0"
120	
121	  downstream_endpoint = "http://vector.vector.svc.cluster.local:4317"
122	  downstream_protocol = "otlp/grpc"
123	}
124	```
125	
126	A complete working example is in [`examples/downstream/`](./examples/downstream/).
127	
128	## Compatibility
129	
130	`v1.1.0` introduces downstream mode. Setting `downstream_endpoint = ""` (the default) preserves identical behavior to `v1.0.x` — no pipeline config, no ExternalSecret logic, and no Helm values change.
131	
132	## Design reference
133	
134	For the full design rationale behind downstream mode and the Vector redaction pipeline, see:  
135	[`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-05-vector-redaction-design.md`](/Users/steve.briggs/projects/IAC/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-05-vector-redaction-design.md) §3.1, §5.1, §5.2
136
